description: Grading engine + exams route layer + module gating + fast tests. The pure deterministic BigInt grading engine (no DB) with exhaustive unit tests, then the full /api/exams route module wired into server.ts with requireModuleActive('examinations') on every route and the fees-verbatim step-up ordering on publish, reusing the attendance-authz marks-scope helpers and the library advisory-lock allocation idiom. Fast mocked route tests keep the fast suite green. Depends on FEAT-001 (needs the deployed tables, the generated Prisma client delegates, the exams.* permission keys, and the exams.* audit keys). Grounded in design.md sections 9-13, 15-17.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/phase8-exams-slice1/design.md (sections 9-13, 15-17) and context.json FIRST, and confirm FEAT-001 landed (schema models present, migration deployed, exams.* permission + audit keys in @campusgate/shared). Do not re-explore what context.json already states.

Implement the pure grading engine in apps/api/src/services/exams/grading.ts per design section 11: integer/BigInt only, export GRADE_POINTS_SCALE = 100, a typed GradingError, and the compute function that accumulates num += (BigInt(marks ?? 0) * BigInt(weight) * 1_000_000n) / BigInt(maxMarks) across assessments, rounds half-up ONCE via percentBps = Number((num + 5_000n) / 10_000n), bands with the pure-integer predicate minPercentBps <= percentBps <= maxPercentBps, copies gradeLabel/gradePoints from the matched band, sets passed = band.isPassing, and throws GradingError on weight-sum != 100 or band gap/no-match. No DB access.

Add apps/api/src/services/exams/__tests__/grading.test.ts covering AC-8 exhaustively: integer basis-point band boundaries, the explicit assertion that the naive Math.round(89.995*100)===8999 float path is NOT taken (a value that must become 9000 does), weight-sum=100 enforcement, zero marks, absent-mark-is-0, 0%/100% extremes, single-assessment subject (weight 100), passed = isPassing including a passing band with gradePoints=0, and the band-gap GradingError.

Implement apps/api/src/routes/exams.ts (export examsRoutes) following the fees.ts/library.ts house pattern: one top-level app.addHook('preHandler', authenticate); gate const = 'examinations'; per-route preHandler [requirePermission(key), requireModuleActive(gate)]; publish uses the VERBATIM fees ordering [requirePermission('exams.results.publish'), requireStepUp('exams.results.publish'), requireModuleActive(gate)]; every handler inside withTenant(institutionId, tx => ...) with institutionId from request.user; Zod on every input; audits via recordAuditEvent. Include an advanceExamStatus(tx, examId, from, to) helper (optimistic where:{id,institutionId,status:from} + trigger backstop). Routes per design section 15: POST/PATCH/GET /exams + GET /exams/:id; POST /exams/:id/status; POST/GET /exams/:id/schedules; POST /exams/:id/schedules/:scheduleId/allocate (capacity-aware, body { candidateIds: string[] }, reuse the library lockStudent idiom SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(${institutionId}:${scheduleId}, 0)), count-under-lock, seatNo server-assigned integer ordinal stored as String(nextOrdinal), partial-unique backstop, already-allocated-elsewhere => 409, already-here => no-op); POST/GET /exams/:id/candidates; POST/PATCH/GET assessments (weight-sum=100 service invariant recomputed in-tx); PUT /exams/:id/marks (accepted ONLY in MARKS_OPEN else 409; REUSE resolveMarkingFaculty + assertFacultyAssigned from attendance-authz.ts VERBATIM, pass the facultyId:'' sentinel; resolve candidate section via ClassEnrollment -> ClassSection WHERE ClassSection.academicTermId = exam.academicTermId; first write => exams.marks.entered + history MARKED, later edit => exams.marks.corrected + history CORRECTED decided by whether a marks_records row exists for (assessmentId, candidateId); out-of-scope => 403 + exams.marks.entered DENIED, no row); GET /exams/:id/marks (exams.results.view); POST /exams/:id/marks/:recordId/correct (ONLY in MODERATION, reason required, exams.marks.corrected {reason} + history CORRECTED); POST/PATCH/GET grading-schemes + bands (validate contiguity nextBand.minPercentBps = prevBand.maxPercentBps + 1, non-overlap, and monotonic-non-decreasing isPassing up the band order); POST /exams/:id/publish (section 9/10 advisory lock on exampub:institutionId:examId, require APPROVED or PUBLISHED else 409, require exactly one isActive GradingScheme else 409, compute per candidate x subject via the engine, INSERT one result_snapshots row each under a new result_publications row with version = max+1 and status PUBLISHED and reason required when version>1, advance APPROVED->PUBLISHED on first publish, audit exams.results.published); GET /exams/:id/results + /results/distribution + /rollups + /results.xlsx (ExcelJS via the admin.ts new ExcelJS.Workbook()/addWorksheet pattern, exams.results.view); GET /me/results + /me/results/:examId (exams.results.view_own, latest PUBLISHED max-version snapshot for the calling student only). Map DB restrict_violation errors to 409 per the design section 16 table.
Register the routes in apps/api/src/server.ts: import { examsRoutes } from './routes/exams.js' and await app.register(examsRoutes, { prefix: '/api/exams' }) next to the existing fees registration.

Add apps/api/src/routes/__tests__/exams.test.ts (fast, mocks @campusgate/db) covering route wiring: permission + module gating, step-up gating on publish (AC-6 fast portion), Zod 400s, marks range 400, weight-sum 400, status-advance 409, publish 409 when not approved / no active scheme.
Run the fast suite and the build and fix any regressions so the fast suite stays fully green.
acceptance_criteria: npm test -w @campusgate/api -- grading passes all AC-8 engine unit tests including the explicit no-Math.round-float assertion.
npm test -w @campusgate/api -- exams passes the new fast route-wiring tests (gating, step-up, Zod/range/weight 400s, status/publish 409s).
npm test -w @campusgate/api stays fully green (454 baseline + the new fast tests; no regressions).
npm run build -w @campusgate/api typechecks with examsRoutes registered at /api/exams.
